value.body: The Master of Vocation (M.Voc) is a two-year, skills-based master's that continues the B.Voc model. It combines classroom study with a large share of practical training, internships and industry projects in one sector — for example IT, media, retail, healthcare, tourism or automobiles. Courses are aligned to the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).

items.label: Students enrolled
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, programme-wise enrolment, all modes (Ministry of Education)

items.label: NSQF level
items.note: Entry usually expects a B.Voc at Level 7

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Voc in the same or a related sector; some institutions also admit other graduates under their own rules. Admission is usually on merit or through the university's entrance test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Few institutions offer it, so choices are limited and may mean moving cities.
Employers in the same sector may value the hands-on training; awareness of the degree is still limited elsewhere.
Staying in the same sector as your B.Voc makes the progression smoother.

value.title: M.Voc enrolment
value.note: 2021-22 lists M.Voc under two programme names (23 + 1,553 students), added together here; later years use one row. AISHE counts only responding institutions, and coverage varies by year, so part of any change can reflect reporting rather than real growth or decline.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 programme-wise enrolment, based on actual responses (Ministry of Education)
